ruleName: Ball hits an outside influence or the player
group: Ball hits an outside influence or the player
imagePrompt: A teen boy on the fairway watches as his golf ball comes to rest after accidentally hitting a dog, holding his iron club, under sunny weather.
imageAlt: Teen boy golfer's ball hits a dog on the fairway.

issues: The golfer's left-handed stance could be slightly more convincing; his right hand may look slightly dominant.
Club grip and posture are mostly natural, but could improve to be more distinctively left-handed.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Ensure the teen boy is holding and addressing the iron golf club in a distinctly left-handed manner (right hand below left on grip, facing the target from the left-handed side). Emphasize natural and physically correct left-handed golf posture.

questions.title: What to Do If Your Ball Hits Someone or an Animal
questions.question: You hit your golf ball and it accidentally bumps into a person or an animal. What should you do next?

choices.text: Add a penalty and hit the shot again
Play your ball from where it stopped, no penalty
Drop a new ball nearby and play from there
Add two extra shots and keep going

questions.explanation: If your golf ball accidentally hits a person or animal, just play your ball from where it stopped. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Extra shots added to your score because of a rule mistake.

vocabulary.term: Play the ball as it lies
vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Hit the ball from where it finished after your shot.

questions.teachingTip: Help kids learn that sometimes things happen by accident in golf, and the rules tell us what to do. Use soft toys or cones for safe practice when showing examples.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they always get a penalty if the ball hits something.
Some might try to hit the shot again instead of playing from where the ball stopped.

questions.title: Playing after your ball hits another person or animal
questions.question: Your golf ball accidentally hits a person or an animal while in play. What does the rule say you should do?

choices.text: Add a penalty and replay the shot
Play the ball as it lies, no penalty
Drop a new ball near where the incident happened
Add two penalty strokes and continue

questions.explanation: If your ball hits a person or animal by chance, you play the ball from where it rests with no penalty.
